title: The Inference Crossing
statement: A mapped city holds the evidence; a bridge carries the necessary leap; an ornamental dark aperture refuses to resolve. The fish, carefully seen yet out of place, marks the fragile passage between knowledge, inference, and the unknowable.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

actions.title: The Inference Crossing
actions.statement: A mapped city holds the evidence; a bridge carries the necessary leap; an ornamental dark aperture refuses to resolve. The fish, carefully seen yet out of place, marks the fragile passage between knowledge, inference, and the unknowable.

notes.note: Establish a tripartite field: a mapped ground for what is documented, a bridge for inference, and a dark ornamental aperture for what remains inaccessible; introduce a precisely observed specimen as a witness moving between them.

actions.title: The Inference Crossing
actions.statement: A mapped city holds the evidence; a bridge carries the necessary leap; an ornamental dark aperture refuses to resolve. The fish, carefully seen yet out of place, marks the fragile passage between knowledge, inference, and the unknowable.

notes.note: Clarify inference as an active mechanism at the seam between the portal and bridge, then set a small natural specimen beside it as evidence that remains partial rather than conclusive.
Refine the fish into a true specimen-like silhouette so the documented witness no longer carries its paper field; this makes its displacement across the mapped lower register more legible.

Add one dark, taxonomic fragment at the far lower edge as an unresolved counterpoint to the brightly documented fish, extending the unknown beyond the central aperture without overcrowding the crossing.
Tighten the documented fish once more, removing the remaining cream paper halo—especially at its tail—so it reads as a clear observation against the map rather than as a pasted rectangular plate.

The completed collage now holds a readable sequence: mapped evidence below, an unstable photographic crossing, a mechanical act of inference at the seam, and a richly framed void whose smaller biological echoes remain unresolved. The balance of precise specimens and withheld interior information satisfies the intended boundary.
